en.title: Maximum Sales Revenue with Prices Set by Remaining Stock
en.description:
Each customer buys exactly one item; the price of a product for that sale equals its remaining stock before the sale, and the stock drops by one afterward. Given m customers, find the maximum revenue, without taking any modulo. The original does not guarantee enough stock, so this site specifies that the output is −1 when the total stock is <m. The explanation of original example 1 misstates the stock; with input [10,10,8,9,1] and m=6, the answer should be 55.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by n values of quantity; full original bounds 1≤n≤100000, 1≤m≤1000000000, 1≤quantity[i]≤1000000000. m≤total stock is not required.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 55; 11; -1. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Sort the stock in descending order and lower the several highest stocks together to the next level; when there are not enough customers to sell off a full level, use division to compute the number of full levels lowered and the leftover sales, and accumulate with arithmetic-series sums.
